decisions.rationale: Test diverse values of the dominant site s1, notably exploring s1=C which conditionally simplifies the space, alongside complementary alternatives on s1 and s5 to map out cost extremes.
s1=A achieved the lowest f1 so far. Exploring variations of s1=A with s2=B, s4=B and different s5 settings to check if f2 can be reduced while keeping low f1.
s1=A combined with s2=B achieves low f2, while s3=B, s4=A, and s5=B strongly drive down f1. Testing s1=A, s2=B, s3=B, s4=A with s5=B could yield a dominant trade-off.
s1=A and s3=B, s4=A consistently yield low f1, while s2=B keeps f2 low. Testing remaining s5 options (D) with this base, and exploring s1=B or D under this promising sub-space.
Sample diverse values across s1 and s5 to map primary cost influences, while flipping binary parameters s2, s3, s4 from the original baseline.
s1=B yielded very low f1 but high f2; testing s1=B with s5=D or s5=E, and s1=E with s2=A/s4=B, to explore trade-offs between low f1 and low f2.
Configurations with s2=A, s3=B, s4=B drastically reduce f1. Pair them with s1=E and s5=E (both linked to low f2) or test s1=C and s5=C to discover new trade-offs along the Pareto front.
s5=E combined with s2=A, s3=B, s4=B dramatically lowers f1, while s5=C is unexplored in this region. Testing s5=C with the best s2-s4 settings and exploring intermediate s2/s4 toggles to reduce f2.
Explore variations of the primary categorical drivers s1 and s5, while toggling binary site options to map the initial objective landscape.
Configuration 4 achieved very low f1 with s1=C and s5=C. Testing s1=C with combinations yielding low f2 (like s5=D or s5=B, and varying s2-s4) to improve trade-offs along the Pareto frontier.
s1=C consistently offers strong trade-offs. Testing s1=C with s5=B/D and intermediate settings like s2=A, s3=A, s4=B balances f1 and f2 to fill gaps along the Pareto front.
Combine label C for s1 (strong for low f1) and B for s3 with varied s2/s4/s5 combinations to probe the intermediate trade-off between f1 (~11k-90k) and f2 (~3k-4.5k).
Initial exploration across primary sites s1 and s5 to identify main effects on f1 and f2 relative to baseline.
Exploration of internal parameters (s2, s3, s4) on top-performing s1 levels (A, D, E) to improve trade-offs along the discovered Pareto frontier.
Combine s1=A and s3=B (which gave low f1 with modest f2 increase) with variations in s4, s2, and s5 to discover improved Pareto trade-offs.
s4=B reduced f1 significantly without hurting f2 much in eval 12. Combining s4=B with low-f1 options (s2=A, s3=B, or s1=D/E) explores potential Pareto breakthroughs.
Explore alternative s1 and s5 settings to assess main effects across the search space while varying binary sites.
Config 6 achieved the best f1 with s1=D, s3=B, s4=B. Blending features of config 1 (lowest f2) and config 6 (lowest f1) targets favorable trade-offs across s2, s5, and s1=B.
s1=B and s2=A achieve the lowest f1, while s2=B optimizes f2. Testing s1=B with s2=B and s5=A may yield very low f2 and f1. Also exploring other s5 levels.
s1=B with s5=A consistently excels. Testing s3=A on low-f1 configurations like s1=B, s2=A, s4=B or testing s4=A on the low-f2 front to balance both objectives.
Explore varied settings across s1 and s5, which have the largest label spaces, along with toggling binary sites to map initial main effects against baseline.
s1=D drastically lowers f1, while s5=E favors low f2. Combining s1=D with various s5 labels explores the frontier between high throughput and low resource usage.

Configuration 11 with s1=D, s2=B, s3=A, s4=B achieved the lowest f1 (4787) when s5=D. Testing s5=A explores further f1/f2 reductions for this favorable sub-branch, while s1=E variants trade f2 for low f1.
Evaluate s1=E and s1=B with s2=B, s3=A, s4=A or s5 variants to find better f1/f2 tradeoffs around the low-f1, moderate-f2 frontier.
Initial exploration across diverse choices of primary sites s1 and s5 to identify strong main effects and establish baselines across the trade-off surface.
Explore combinations of s1=C and s1=E with varied intermediate sites s2-s4 and low-cost s5 labels (A, C, D) to find solutions dominating the current front between f1=37k and 91k.
s1=C with s3=B, s4=B yields very low f1; testing s2=B with s5=C or s5=B may reduce f2 below 6784 while keeping f1 minimal. Exploring s2 combinations on s1=C.
s1=C with s2=B, s3=B gives low f1, while s2=A gives lower f2. Evaluating s5=E with s1=C and combinations of s2/s3/s4 explores new optimal trade-offs in the front.
Initial exploration across primary sites s1 and s5 to identify strong main effects relative to the baseline.
Explore effects of s2, s3, and s4 variations on promising s1 values (B, C, D) and investigate remaining s5 options to balance f1 and f2 trade-offs.
s3=A yielded a major f1 reduction with modest f2 increase in #8. We test s3=A with s1=C and s1=A, and explore the effect of unmeasured site s4=B.
s4=B combined with s3=B or s3=A yielded strong f1 reductions. Testing s1=A with s4=B can explore low f2 regions, while s2=A with s4=B could push f1 even lower.
Sample diverse values across top-level sites s1 and s5 to explore the global space and test s1 variants, including conditional masking when s1=E.
Config 6 achieved very low f1 with s5=E. We test if s5=E combined with minimal f2 settings (such as s1=B or s1=A and base labels for s2-s4) can achieve strong trade-offs or lower f2.
s5=E strongly optimizes both objectives when combined with s2/s3/s4. With s1=A and s1=B, toggling subsets of s2, s3, s4 explores intermediate trade-offs between f1=4836 and f2=1984.
Focus on s5=E where both objectives thrive. Exploring combinations like s2=A, s3=B, s4=B on s1=D and s1=A with intermediate subsets like s3=B or s4=B can yield superior trade-offs.
Explore varied values across major sites s1 and s5, and alter s2-s4 settings to evaluate label sensitivities relative to the baseline configuration.
s5=A and s4=A appear strongly across the Pareto front. Combining s1=E or s1=A with the favorable s2=B, s3=B configuration explores lower f1 with reduced f2.
s2=B, s3=B, s4=A yields low f1, while s2=A, s3=A gives lower f2. Evaluating s3=A with s2=B or s4=B explores the intermediate trade-off along s1=A and s1=E.
s2=B, s3=B, s4=A, s5=A gives optimal f1 across s1 variants. Testing unexplored s5 values (B, C, D) on the high-performing backbone (s1=E/A, s2=B, s3=B, s4=A) may yield better trade-offs.
